title: Declarative event envelopes and concise invocation contracts for SDKs (TS/Py/Go)
creator: Asha Reddy
description:
Problem: The current SDK examples and interfaces for streaming + tool invocation have a lot of ad-hoc shapes across TypeScript, Python, and Go. That makes cross-language examples fragile and increases support burden when evolving streaming envelopes (progress events, partial tool results, final structured payloads).

Goal: Define a compact, declarative event envelope and a concise invocation contract that can be generated or hand-coded idiomatically in each language. Deliverables: (1) spec doc for the envelope and invocation lifecycle, (2) reference implementations in TS/Py/Go with examples (stream + tool call + structured output), (3) migration guide for existing SDK consumers, (4) tests and interop matrix.

Scope: Focus on the runtime invocation surface (start -> progressive events -> tool calls -> structured final). Do not change wire protocol; this is an SDK-level compatibility/UX layer. Provide backward-compatible helpers that can be opt-in and a strict mode for new projects.
acceptance_criteria: A single spec (human readable) describing event envelope fields and semantics is published to Confluence
TypeScript, Python, and Go reference packages expose idiomatic constructors/parsers for the envelope
End-to-end example (chat with two tool calls + streaming partials + final JSON schema output) provided for each language
Automated interop tests demonstrate identical event sequences between TS/Py/Go against a local test harness
Migration guide with 3 common migration recipes (stream-only, tools-only, mixed) is available
No breaking changes to existing wire protocol; helpers are opt-in by default
comments: 2025-02-10 - Asha Reddy: Kickoff: drafted problem statement and rough envelope fields. Shared Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SDK/Declarative+Envelopes. Assigned to Marco for implementation planning.

2025-02-12 - Marco Liu: Initial design meeting notes - we converged on a small envelope: {type, id, timestamp, payload, meta}. Decided that tool-result fragments will use type="tool.partial" and final structured outputs use type="output.structured". Added compatibility hooks for older stream parsers.

2025-02-14 - Nina Park (SDK): Created TypeScript prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/1024. Prototype shows StreamEnvelope class with fromJSON / asEvent helpers. Requesting API review from @design and @runtime.

2025-02-16 - Runtime team review (Daniel Ortega): Concern about KV cache ordering in presence of interleaved tool.partial events; proposed adding sequence_id and optional session_id fields to envelope meta. Marked action item to update spec and add test cases.

2025-02-18 - Marco Liu: Implemented Python and Go parsers, added basic interop tests. Open PRs: TS #1024, Py #204, Go #37. Running cross-language harness locally; two failing cases around incremental JSON concatenation for tool.partial. Next: resolve concatenation semantics and document in migration guide.
notes: Trade-offs: Keep the envelope minimal to avoid SDK bloat vs. adding fields that make interop simpler. We favored minimal + extensible meta map.
Decision: Opt-in helpers rather than global switch to avoid surprising behavior for existing customers.
Trade-offs: We will not change wire-level framing now. Any future wire changes require a migration window and release coordination.
